source_text: Sed de bono facere meliores; atque ad unum quidem collem omnes, quos susceperit, sanctificationis evehere, sed non omnes in eadem vitiorum palude deprehendere, verum alios invenire in statu innocentium, alios in studiis noxiorum. Hoc ergo quia dicimus, quod fidei sanitate, praesidio rationis atque intellegentiae pietate munitur, per quod et Christi gratia iure laudatur nec Deo applicatur ullus reatus, tu dicis auctoritatem nutare sacramenti atque acumine pistillo omni obtunsiore asseris auferri auctoritatem gratiae, nisi ei calumniandi flagitium adscribatur, nisi iustitiae instituta perverterit, nisi his, qui scientiam non habent, alienae conscientiae crimen impegerit, postremo nihil eam efficere, si non in omnibus uniformiter praedicetur operari.
pass_a_gloss: But from the good to make better; and to lift all whom it has taken up to one hill of sanctification, but not to catch all in the same marsh of vices, but to find some in the state of innocents, others in the pursuits of the noxious. This therefore because we say, which is fortified by the soundness of faith, the protection of reason, and the piety of understanding, through which both the grace of Christ is rightly praised and no reatus is applied to God, you say that the authority of the sacrament totters and by a sharpness blunter than every pestle you assert that the authority of grace is taken away, unless the shameful act of slandering is ascribed to it, unless it has perverted the ordinances of justice, unless it has driven the crime of another's conscience upon those who do not have knowledge, finally that it effects nothing, if it is not preached to work uniformly in all.

lemmas.lexica: LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: Instead, it makes the good better. It raises everyone it receives to the same summit of sanctification, but does not find everyone in the same swamp of vices. It finds some in the condition of the innocent, others engaged in wrongdoing. This is what we say, protected by sound faith, reason’s support, and reverent understanding. Through it Christ’s grace is rightly praised and no guilt is attributed to God. Yet you say the sacrament’s authority totters. With a sharpness blunter than any pestle, you assert that grace loses its authority unless the crime of slander is attributed to it, unless it overturns the institutions of justice, unless it charges those without knowledge with the guilt of another’s conscience. Finally, you say it accomplishes nothing unless it is proclaimed to operate uniformly in everyone.

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: In this book Julian usually means the Savior's gift abounding against Adam's sin (Rom 5), not later system-grace as a substance, and not 'favoritism' unless a suum-cuique definition is in play.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
